strings.m.title: Foreign-disc intake, offline — Singapore clinics and hospitals
strings.m.meta_desc: Read the imaging CDs international patients bring, organize the studies and hand them to your team — offline, nothing sent anywhere. Free 60-day pilot.
strings.m.og_desc: Read the imaging CDs international patients bring and hand your team the studies, fully offline. Procurement kit ready; free 60-day pilot.
strings.m.uc_lead: For private specialist and imaging clinics, hospital international-patient centres, and hospitals in Johor that care for patients from Singapore.
strings.m.currency_note: Prices are in US dollars (USD). Ask us if you need a quote in SGD.
strings.m.procurement_note: Pay by card online (opening soon) or ask us for an invoice. Responding to a public-sector tender? Email us.

use_cases.title: Foreign-disc intake
use_cases.text: Patients arrive with CDs from hospitals across the region. Read each disc at the front desk and hand your team one organized set of studies instead of a pile of discs.

use_cases.title: Complete studies before arrival
use_cases.text: Referred patients can consolidate their own discs onto one USB drive with MIA Toolkit — free for patients — so the specialist has complete studies from the first visit.

use_cases.title: Care across the Causeway
use_cases.text: For patients whose care spans Johor and Singapore, one standard DICOMDIR on USB travels with them between both sides.

compliance.text: The app collects and transmits nothing: studies are processed on your workstation and no personal data reaches us.
HSA GL-04-R4 (Dec 2025): software that only stores, converts or transfers images is not a medical device. MIA Toolkit stores, converts and transfers studies; it never interprets or measures them.
Expected to take effect in early 2027. Listed for context only; we will update this row when its requirements apply.
